proposals.evidence: DEDR 1942 explicitly lists Tamil/Malayalam keṭṭa and Kannada keṭṭa bad or spoiled, beside the ruin/spoil verb. The selected adjective and neuter forms fit these attested senses; negative phrases meaning not good and unrelated loan adjectives are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

These simple dry stems and ordinary inflections are selected; causative verb phrases and the distinctive Toda forms require separate analysis. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4889 gives Tamil/Malayalam mukam, Kannada moga/mōṟe, Tulu mōrè, and Gondi mokom/mukam face. The selected simple face stems match this family; mūñci/mond- responses belong to a separate family and are not merged. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
